Communication · 01

Measure the impact of an event or campaign, beyond the views.

A launch, a sponsorship, a keynote: reach figures tell you how many people saw it. They do not tell you what changed in their minds. We read the conversation before and after, audience by audience, to tell you what the campaign actually moved.

Book a meeting →

The questions we answer

  • Did our campaign change the way people talk about us?
  • Which audiences reacted, and which ones stayed indifferent?
  • Who carried the message: our content, creators, the press?
  • What do we do again, and what do we stop?

What you get

  • A before / after read of the conversation, broken down by audience and platform.
  • The peaks explained: who triggered them, with which content.
  • The comparison with your category's average.
  • Three recommendations for the next campaign.

What we read

  • Social networksTikTok, Instagram, X, LinkedIn, YouTube, Facebook: posts, comments, shares.
  • Press and blogsPick-ups, angles, the headlines that travelled.
  • SearchThe searches the campaign triggered, before and after.
  • Generative AIWhat assistants now answer when asked about your brand.

How we go about it

  1. 01Framing

    We set the baseline period, the campaign's goals and the audiences that matter.

  2. 02Collection

    We collect the conversation before, during and after, across every relevant platform.

  3. 03Analysis

    An analyst reads the peaks, themes and voices, and compares with your category's average.

  4. 04Decision

    We walk you through what worked, what did not land, and what we would change next time.

An example

Illustrative example: a food brand launches a sauce with a TV campaign. The conversation shows that creators' recipes on TikTok carried the launch, not the ad. Recommendation: move part of the media budget to creator partnerships.

Frequently asked questions

How soon after the campaign can you measure?

A first read is possible as soon as the campaign ends; a full read takes a few days.

Do you also measure physical events?

Yes: trade shows, sponsorships, conferences. What counts is what they got people saying online, and who.

Can you compare several campaigns?

Yes, with the same method and baseline, to know which one really moved the conversation.
